newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court finds Luxembourg late to enact environment rules.
newsitem.headline: Court finds Luxembourg late to enact environment rules.

text.p: The European Court of Justice found on Thursday the Duchy of Luxembourg was late to enact Community rules on genetically modified micro-organisms.

Luxembourg did not deny that it failed to transpose directives governing modified micro-organisms, but claimed the delay was related both to the complexity of the subject-matter and to the discussion on the draft implementing legislation during the consultation process.

The court has consistently held that a member state may not plead provisions, practices or circumstances exising in its internal legal system to justify a failure to comply with the obligations and time-limits laid down by a directive.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: French)
"Failure to fulfil obligations - Council directives 90/219/EEC and 90/220/EEC - Genetically modified organisms"
Commission of the European Communities, applicant

application for a declaration that, by failing to adopt within the prescribed period the measures necessary in order to comply with Council directive 90/219/EEC of 23 April 1990 on the contained use of technically modified micro-organisms (OJ 1990 L 117, p. 1), and Council directive 90/220/EEC of 23 April 1990 on the deliberate release into the environment of genetically modified organisms (OJ 19990 L 117, p. 15), the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg has failed to fulfil its obligations under articles 22 and 23 of those directives respectively and under articles 5 and 189 of the EC Treaty.

1. Declares that, by failing to adopt within the prescribed period the measures necessary in order to comply with Council directive 90/219/EEC of 23 April 1990 on the contained use of technically modified micro-organisms and Council directive 90/220/EEC of 23 April 1990 on the deliberate release into the environment of genetically modified organisms, the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg has failed to fulfil its obligations under articles 22 and 23 of those directives respectively;
2. Orders the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg to pay the costs.
